claims.text: The equipment components are made from a base metal such as steel.
An alumina (Al2O3) ceramic coating can be applied by plasma spraying.
The hot-dip aluminum plating environment reaches temperatures up to 700°C.
The alumina coating enhances resistance to corrosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The alumina coating increases the service life of the equipment components.
The alumina coating forms a barrier that prevents direct contact between liquid aluminum and the base metal.
Preventing direct contact between liquid aluminum and the base metal reduces corrosion.
Alumina-coated components will have a 50% longer service life than uncoated components.
The proposed operating boundary is 600°C to 800°C with exposure to liquid aluminum for up to 1000 hours.
Service-life improvement may depend on process conditions, coating thickness, and coating adhesion.
Uncoated steel components are the proposed experimental control.
The hypothesis is falsified if coated components fail to achieve at least a 30% service-life increase after 500 hours compared with uncoated components.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that process temperatures are up to 700°C, whereas the stated applicability boundary extends to 800°C without explaining the additional 100°C range.
